name: The Belly of the Beast
title: The Belly of the Beast: Human Blood Under the Scarecrow, a Door Burned Shut, and the Skittering Grove Inside the Tree
date: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF — continuing the same storm-night, from the grove into the tree
era: Harvestide 1040 BF — Shadow Estate storm chain
location: The overgrown grove beyond Tymnas's cottage, and the Skittering Grove inside the Scorncrow's tree (Shadowfell)
status: Unresolved — the party is inside the Skittering Grove, the jaws are shut, the exit Archie made is sealed, Remi is webbed and separated, and there are Legion soldiers in there with them
summary: The Scorncrow put Feyward Dan down with a murder of crows, Archie slammed it out of the air onto Remi, and Remi — pinned at point-blank range — fired a musket into its face and found human blood. The thing fled into the mouth of its own tree; the party followed, Archie sealed the only exit burning it, Markop pried the jaws open and rigged a rope, and five of them descended into the Skittering Grove: a web-canopied grove inside the tree, hung with wrapped bodies, full of ettercaps, giant green spiders, and Legion soldiers.
description:
*Waluigi has filed three engagements against the Scorncrow. In every one of them the thing shouted that it was not a monster and Waluigi wrote that down as villain theatre, because that is what it sounds like. On the night of 30 Harvestide a fourteen-year-old girl pinned under its body pressed a musket to its face and fired, and the face came off, and the blood underneath was human. This article is partly a correction. WAH!*

The battle continued out of the grove skirmish without a pause. Crows took Feyward Dan down unconscious at Archie's feet; Salam crossed open ground to stabilise him; Archie planted his staff and shook the earth, and the Scorncrow's crows simply lifted it off the ground that was failing. It offered a swing — pointed, spiked — and Archie answered by slamming it out of the air knowing full well it would land on Remi. It did. She shot it in the face at zero range.

Wario cleared the shadow servants, freed his motorbike, and rode at everything. The Scorncrow laughed and jumped into the mouth of its own tree. Then the plans came apart: Archie argued for withdrawal and immediately talked himself into arson, Remi honked a horn that laughed in Wario's voice across a fifty-mile radius, Feyward Dan healed himself with every point of magic he owned and reported — inside an insult — that they had not seen half the Scorncrow's power.

Wario rode into the mouth. Remi went in after. Both ended up in cobwebs with the motorbike gone. Archie, outside and unanswered, poured every reserve he had into one weakened fire cast until his eyes turned to fire, and killed the tree, and sealed the exit doing it. Markop pulled a piece of bark and the jaws shut. Then he pried them open again, found a pit, tested it with a torch — and the pit answered, in voices, saying someone was going to burn them all down.

They set a marching order with reasons attached, went down Markop's rope, and arrived in the Skittering Grove.
imageCaption: The mask in flight. Knocked off at point-blank range, it tumbles away trailing straw — and underneath is an ordinary human face. Three filings called this thing a monster on its own denial; this is the moment the denial was tested.

sections.name: I. The Crows Take Feyward Dan
sections.overview:
The crows came off the branches all at once, and the sound they made was not a caw. It was a dry, leathery clatter, a thousand playing cards shuffled at speed, and it went up into the dark and then bent sideways and came down on Feyward Dan.

He got one arm up. That was all the time there was. The mass closed over his red cap and his mail and the shape of him disappeared into a churn of black wings and small hooking beaks, and the noise from inside it was the noise of hail on a tin roof — beaks on steel, over and over, working the gaps in the rings.

"GET OFF —" he said, and then he stopped saying anything.

The birds lifted. They went up in a single spiral, unhurried, the way smoke leaves a chimney, and Feyward Dan came down on his face in the churned mud at Archie Miser's boots. A feather turned over in the air above him and took a long time to land. One of his gauntlets had come off. His fingers moved once and did not move again.

Archie did not look down at him for long. He looked across the grove, at the tall ragged thing standing in the middle of it with straw at its cuffs, and he shouted over his shoulder without turning his head.

"SALAM."

Salam was behind a fallen trunk forty feet back with his hands flat on the wood. He looked at Dan. He looked at the scarecrow. He looked at the forty feet of open churned ground between the two, and he did the arithmetic out loud in a voice that had gone up half an octave.

"Alright — but keep that thing distracted. It's kinda scary."

Then he came over the trunk. He ran badly, low and hunched with his arms tucked, mushroom cap bobbing, the way people run when they expect the sky to be the thing that kills them. He dropped onto his knees in the mud so hard he skidded, and he got both hands under Dan's shoulder and rolled him over out of the wet.

*"Your service won't go in vain,"* Salam said — to a man who was still breathing, which is either the wrong thing to say or the truest thing anyone said all night — and got to work.
sections.waluigi_note: Read the target selection, because it is the whole night in one move. Three engagements this squad has fought, and the Scorncrow opened the fourth by removing the healer before it touched anybody else. That is not a swarm finding a body. That is something that has watched them fight and knows which one to take off the board first.

sections.name: II. Something Really Risky
sections.overview:
"I'm doing something really risky," Archie announced.

Nobody had time to ask which part. He was already running — cloak snapping, boots throwing up wet leaf-litter, the third eye on his forehead wide open and fixed on the scarecrow. Ten paces out he stopped dead, reversed the staff in both hands, and drove it into the earth like a man setting a fence post.

The ground answered. It went first with a deep grinding sound, felt in the teeth before it was heard, and then the whole floor of the grove humped and split. Roots tore up out of the soil, pale and wet. Stones stood on end. The dead leaves jumped an inch off the ground and came down again in a wave that travelled outward from the staff and broke against the tree.

The Scorncrow watched all this happen. Then it laughed — a wet, comfortable sound, like a boot pulling out of mud.

*"Oh, you little thing."*

And the crows came in under its arms. They took it up off the buckling earth, a dozen of them at each shoulder, and it hung there in the air with its heels a foot clear of everything Archie had just broken, tattered coat-tails swinging gently over ground that was still shaking itself apart underneath.

Then it tipped its sacking head to one side, the way you do when you are being polite to a child.

"Care for a swing?"

Above Remi, a branch turned. It came down out of the canopy on a slow creaking arc, thick as a man's thigh, and the end of it was not blunt — it had been split lengthwise into a point, four feet of pale splintered wood, and it was descending exactly where a person's chest would be.

Archie did not shout a warning and he did not dodge. He ran three steps, jumped, and hit the Scorncrow with his shoulder and all of his weight.

He knew, leaving the ground, where the thing was going to land. Remi was standing right there. He could see her. He connected anyway.
sections.waluigi_note: Archie keeps attacking the Scorncrow's relationship with the ground, and the Scorncrow keeps proving it does not have one. Twice now he has broken the earth under a thing that is carried. The crows are not decoration and they are not a mood — they are the landing gear, and until somebody grounds the birds, every tremor he casts is an expensive way to redecorate a field.

sections.name: III. Point Blank, and What Was Under the Face
sections.overview:
The Scorncrow went over backwards. It did not fall like a person falls — it folded, slow and wrong, more sailcloth than body, and it came down across Remi Akamatsu and put her flat in the mud underneath it.

"I'll make sure it's worth it," Archie said, to nobody.

Forty feet away, Wario had both fists on the handlebars of the motorbike and one boot braced against the front wheel, hauling. The rear tyre was buried past the axle in wet dirt. The shadow servants came in around him in a loose ring, unhurried, and he did not look up at them once. He kept pulling.

Eager came in on the fallen Scorncrow with the Shadow Blade lit in his fist and brought it down in a flat silver arc — and stopped it, hard, mid-swing, with his whole body twisting to kill the momentum. The tip passed maybe a hand's width over Remi's shoulder. He backed off three steps with the blade held wide and away, breathing through his teeth.

Underneath several hundred pounds of straw and wet coat, Remi took stock.

"Well, I have this monster on top of me. I'd better get him off of me."

"Preferably push him onto the tremor I made earlier," Archie called.

She got a shoulder into it and shoved. Nothing moved. "It's too heavy."

Then she went quiet. When she spoke again it was flat and small and entirely practical, the voice of somebody who has run out of options and found the last one lying on top of her.

*"Wait a minute. I'm at point-blank range."*

She worked the musket up between her chest and the thing's face, pressed the muzzle into the sacking, turned her head away, and fired.

The bang went flat and huge across the grove. Grey powder smoke rolled out sideways. The burlap mask came off the head entire, tumbling away through the smoke trailing straw and one loose thread, and it landed face-up in the mud six feet away with its painted stitched grin pointing at the sky.

**[[prop:prop_scorncrow_unmasking_note|Underneath it was a face. Pale. Sunken. Human. And it was bleeding the way a man bleeds.]]**

Remi lay under it and looked up at it and did not say anything at all.
sections.waluigi_note: Three filings. Three times that thing has stood in a field and shouted *I am not a monster*, and three times Waluigi wrote the word monster in the very next sentence. A fourteen-year-old pinned under its weight tested the claim at a range of zero inches, because it was the only move she had left, and the claim held. The archive was not lied to. The archive was not listening.
sections.imageCaption: What the musket revealed: the burlap mask tumbling away, and a plain, tired, human face beneath it.

sections.name: IV. Wario Clears the Field and the Scorncrow Leaves It
sections.overview:
Wario let go of the motorbike, turned around, and hit the nearest shadow servant so hard it stopped existing. It came apart into a puff of grey ash that hung in the air and drifted. He took the second one on the backswing. Same puff, same drift, ash settling on his shoulder-spikes like grey snow.

"You shadow chumps have nothing on Wario."

Markop came through the rest at a canter with the warhammer swinging low and level, and hooves and hammer between them put the last of the servants down into dust. For a moment the grove held nothing upright but the party and the thing they had spent all night failing to pin.

Then the motorbike came free with a sucking crack, and Wario was on it and moving — full throttle across the churned ground, headlamp swinging wild, straight at the place where Remi and Archie and the unmasked Scorncrow all were.

The Scorncrow got up. It laughed once with its ruined face, turned, and ran three loping strides at the base of the great tree — and the trunk opened for it. A seam split from root to twenty feet up, bark peeling back in long strips, and behind it there was nothing at all. Black, and a smell of wet rot rolling out. The thing went into it head-first and was gone, and the seam ground shut behind it.

The tree had a mouth. Nobody in the grove said anything for a second.

"Thanks for the ride," Archie said to the motorbike that had not arrived yet. Then, more quietly, and more sensibly than anything he would say for the rest of the night: if we can't win this, we run. Dan goes somewhere safe. Where is Green T? *He seems too powerful* — and the giant was not there to ask.

Wario spat. "We can't let him get away." He jabbed a gauntlet at the ground where Dan lay. That toad's poisoned. Look at him — he's *purple*. Send him away.

Then, over the idling engine: "We should go to the belly of the beast, and uproot it."

Remi said it plainer. If the tree has to die, we go inside and kill it from in there.

And Archie — who has never once in the record declined a chance to set something enormous on fire — stopped arguing for the withdrawal.
sections.waluigi_note: Two plans went on the table and they were the same plan in different hats: Wario's uprooting and Remi's arson both required walking into the thing. The third option had already been said out loud, by Archie, thirty seconds earlier, and it was the right one. Nobody voted it down. He simply talked himself out of it, because the alternative involved fire and he is who he is.

sections.name: V. WAHAHAHAH (Fifty Miles)
sections.overview:
They counted heads by torchlight and came up one giant short. No Green T. No note, no shout, no huge footprints leading anywhere — just an absence where the largest thing in the grove had been standing an hour ago.

Archie, surveying a poisoned Toad, an escaped monster and a sealed tree, proposed that they go and celebrate.

"Green T has his own agenda," Wario said, not worried. "Maybe he's helping some other way."

And then Remi, standing beside the idling motorbike, found the horn and pressed it.

**WAHAHAHAH.**

It was not a honk. It was Wario's own laugh, brass-throated and enormous, blasting out of a chrome trumpet on the handlebars at a volume that flattened the grass. It bounced off the tree. It came back off the hills behind the tree. Crows went up out of the canopy in three separate places. The sound rolled away downhill through the dark and kept going for a long time.

"Wow, that's loud," Archie said.

Then he did the arithmetic and his face changed. "Too loud. Fifty mile radius will hear this."

Behind them, in the mud, Feyward Dan sat up.

He had his hands pressed flat to his own chest and a faint white light was going out between his fingers. The peck-wounds closed over as they watched. He got one knee under himself, then the other, and stood up wobbling, and announced at full volume:

"IT'S OKAY ARCHIE, I AM HEALED! I used magic and everything" — and here his voice dropped to almost nothing — *"although I used all of it"* — and came straight back up — "but it's alright, no need to worry!"

Then he turned on Wario and pointed.

"Wow, this guy is going to be a tough fight." He said it grinning, mocking, a paladin who had been unconscious four minutes earlier. "We all should be in this together. You can't handle this on your own." And then, still grinning: **"I don't think that was half his power."**

Wario's answer was to twist the throttle until the engine screamed, put his head down, and ride at the tree. The seam split open ahead of him and the mouth came apart wide.

"NO ONE CHALLENGES WARIO TO A FIGHT AND GETS A-WAY FROM IT!"

The dark took the headlamp, then the engine noise, then all of it.
sections.waluigi_note: *I used all of it* and *that was not half his power* were said by the same Toad, to the same audience, inside the same thirty seconds. One is a report on the party's reserves and the other is a report on the enemy's. Both are catastrophic and both were delivered as a joke, and not one person in that grove changed a single element of the plan.
sections.imageCaption: "No one challenges Wario to a fight and gets a-way from it!" — the motorbike, freed at last, going straight into a mouth that opens to receive it.

sections.name: VI. Cobwebs, and the Wizard Who Sealed the Door
sections.overview:
"Dang," Archie said.

He cupped his hands. "REMI! WARIO! WHERE ARE YOU?"

The grove gave him back nothing — not an echo, not the engine, not a voice. He decided, correctly for once, that this was the tree's fault.

Inside, it was worse than silence. Remi had come down in something soft and yielding that gave under her boots like rotten netting, and when she tried to move her forearm it stayed where it was. Web. Grey cabled stuff, thick as rope in places, strung floor to ceiling in a room with no visible ceiling. The motorbike was not there. Not fallen, not stuck — *gone*, engine and headlamp and all, swallowed somewhere ahead into the dark.

Something came down a strand above her, in stages, with a click at the end of each stage.

"Oh no. Please don't."

It got closer. She tore her arm free with a sound like fabric ripping, went backwards, and the fangs came down where her shoulder had been. Then she was running — badly, in the dark, off-balance — and her boot went through a floor of silk and she pitched forward into the web and stuck fast.

Outside, Archie levelled his staff and put a bolt of fire into the trunk.

It hit with a crack. Bark blackened in a patch the size of a shield and a little smoke curled off it. The tree did not react at all.

He fired again. The same patch went blacker. Nothing else happened.

So the wizard stopped experimenting. He set his feet, planted the staff, and pulled — everything, every reserve he had, weakened as it was in this place, dragged up through his arms and into one cast. The light climbed his sleeves. The third eye blazed. And then his eyes went, both of them, pupils gone, two sockets of open flame throwing shadows up his own face.

The blast hit the trunk and the tree **exploded** inward, fire running up the inside of the seam, and every peeled strip of bark at the mouth curled in on itself and fused into a solid, smoking, welded scar.

The tree died. The door died with it.

"What have you done?" Markop said. "You've destroyed our only entrance."

Archie was already thinking out loud — move the bark over, maybe, or enlarge the tree — while Markop simply took hold of a loose plate of bark at the seam and pulled it away.

The jaws slammed shut.

Somewhere on the other side of them, in the dark, Wario started running.
sections.waluigi_note: Fire bolt: nothing. Second bolt: nothing. Everything he had: the tree dies and the door welds shut. Then Markop pulls one plate of bark and the jaws close harder. Two men, opposite methods, one minute apart, and the opening got smaller both times. Waluigi has stopped thinking of it as a door that is jammed.
sections.imageCaption: Every reserve he had, in one weakened cast, until his eyes turned to fire. The tree died. So did the exit. Markop recoils behind him.

sections.name: VII. Inside: Crows, Webs, and a Guard With a Spear
sections.overview:
What happened inside is a combat log, and Waluigi files it as one, because the people in it did not have the luxury of a story.

The Scorncrow came out of the dark already multiattacking — and it did not go for the man. It went for the machine. **Murder of Crows**, twice, sixteen to hit at disadvantage, feathers boiling out of the black around the motorbike and fourteen points of damage torn out of a thing made of steel. Chrome went. Spokes went. Then it turned on the owner: two more, seventeen and thirteen, and Wario disappeared inside a churning column of wings.

Then **Shadow Jump**, a bonus action, and it simply was not standing there any more.

The grove joined in behind it, and it came in bold. *Ettercap morale: BOLD (84).* Multiattack, and a dash straight at Remi, long limbs moving over the web faster than anything with that many joints should. *Giant Green Spider: BOLD (84)* — a **Web** at a guard, DC 12 Strength, and the man went over sideways with his legs bound to his chest. A second spider rushed the same guard and webbed him again where he lay.

The ettercap broke off Remi and dashed at Wario. Then it changed its mind, spun, and cast **Web Strand** at the guard — DC 12 Dexterity — and **Reeled** him in on the line as a bonus action, hauling a grown man across the floor of the grove on a rope of spit.

Then it went back for Remi and webbed her. Twice.

*Wario retreated from Remi's position.* The log gives no reason but one word: morale.

And the guard — flat on his back, wrapped twice, dragged in on a string, with no name recorded anywhere in this file — got an arm loose, set the spear, and put five points into the ettercap standing over him.

That is the only friendly attack in the entire interior log.
sections.waluigi_note: It attacked the motorbike first. Not the rider — the wheels. Something in that tree identified this party's only means of leaving and destroyed it before laying a claw on the man sitting on it, and then it Shadow Jumped clear before anyone could answer. Waluigi has been filing that thing as a prankster with a scythe. It is a tactician, and it has been taking notes for three engagements.

sections.name: VIII. The Torch Test, and the Voices That Answered It
sections.overview:
Markop got both hands into the welded seam and pulled. Wood shrieked. The jaws came apart maybe four feet and stayed there, quivering, held open on a centaur's shoulders.

Inside was darkness. He put his head into it and looked down, and the darkness kept going — past the roots, past anything a torch could reach, a shaft dropping away into the ground under the grove.

"Anyone have a rope?" Markop asked.

"I don't think soooo," said Dan.

So they [[prop:prop_belly_torch_test|measured it the way you measure a hole]] when you have nothing to measure it with. Somebody lit a torch, leaned over the gap, and dropped it in.

They waited for the sound of it landing. It never came.

*Inside*, though, in the dark, in the webs, Remi heard something else entirely — voices, several of them, close and panicking and talking over each other:

> *"There's a fire —"*
> *"Someone is causing a fire —"*
> *"They're going to burn us all down!"*

And then the torch came back out. Not up through the jaws where it had gone in — it popped out of a split in the *trunk*, six feet to the left, and dropped smoking into the mud at Markop's hooves, still lit.

Nobody outside heard a single word. They looked at the returned torch and read it as a pit being unhelpful.

Then Markop set [[prop:prop_belly_marching_order|the marching order]], and he gave his reasons out loud, which is more than anyone else did all night:

> **Feyward Dan** — paladin. Front.
> **Eager** — scout.
> **Archie** — squishy. Middle.
> **Salam.**
> **Markop** — rear, and the rope is his.

He braced against the trunk, took two turns of hemp around his own barrel, and paid it out hand over hand into the hole. One by one they went down past the bark teeth into the belly of the beast.
sections.waluigi_note: Somebody in that hole said *us*. Not a shriek, not noise — a plural. Whatever is down there can hear a fire, work out that a person caused it, guess what that person intends, and describe itself as a group with a shared fate. The party dropped a torch into a pit to find the bottom and got a coherent objection back, and only one of them was on the right side of the wood to hear it.
sections.imageCaption: The jaws pried open, Markop's rope going down into a pit a thrown torch could not measure, and Remi's torch — the only light anyone brought to it.

sections.name: IX. The Skittering Grove
sections.overview:
Markop's hooves came down on grey earth, and he stopped.

He did not stop the way you stop in a new place. He stopped the way you stop in a room you have been in before and did not expect to be in again — weight going back off the front hooves, head coming up, one long look across the whole span of it before he said anything at all.

"I know this place."

Nobody answered him, because nobody else did.

> At the heart of this skittering grove is a great, towering tree with vast branches reaching out to form a massive canopy over the area. Its boughs are coated in thick webs that are an unnerving mockery of foliage, and hanging from them are the forms of wrapped creatures, both beast and man, dangling like macabre fruit.
>
> This tree is long dead, some terrible malady having killed it from the inside out years ago. Now its dark roots jut from grey earth which no longer nourishes it, as its great arms serve as home to an unimaginable host of creeping, crawling arachnids that accost anything which foolishly wanders into their domain.

There was no sky. That was the first thing. Overhead, where weather should be, there was the ribbed inner wall of a trunk going up and up into green-grey murk — and under it a whole dead forest, standing inside a tree that had been growing in a field an hour ago.

The bundles turned slowly on their threads. Some were the size of a dog. Some were not.

Markop was not looking at the bundles. He walked forward eight or nine paces with the rope still over his shoulder, past the roots, and stopped again at a broad flat stump about four feet across, its top scarred pale where an axe had once gone into it and been pulled back out.

He put a hand flat on it.

This was the Silent Grove. This was the stump they had piled the loot on after they put the Arachnid Matriarch down — the War Mage's Staff that Markop had claimed on Archie's behalf and carried out himself, the Web-Woven Scale, the three healing potions Rodger had grabbed like a man counting his own heartbeats. Same grove. Same tree. Same stump. They had walked out of this place in daylight through open woodland on Raventree Manor's northwestern boundary, and they had just come back into it on a rope, through the jaws of a scarecrow's tree, in the Shadowfell.

"This is the Silent Grove," Markop said. "We cleared it."

Remi loosed an arrow at a spider on a strand and missed, and the shaft went off into the webbing and made no sound landing.

"It seems like I hear someone yelling," she said.

"WHERE ARE YOU!" Markop shouted, and the grove ate it — the same way it had eaten sound the first time, silk taking the edges off every noise until shouting was a thing you did for your own benefit.

Archie stood at the bottom of the rope and thought about spells, which is what a wizard does when he has spent every one of them.

Then Markop found the motorbike. It was lying on its side in the roots at the foot of the great tree, headlamp cracked, chrome dulled with dust, perfectly intact. He stood over it for a while. He is a centaur. There was no arrangement of centaur and motorbike that worked, and both of them knew it.

"If there is a will, there is a way," Archie said, unhelpfully.

Spiders everywhere, on every strand, at every height.

And, in among them, moving in a formation that spiders do not use: **Legion soldiers.**

Remi took stock of the situation and identified the only objective that mattered — figuring out how not to die.
sections.waluigi_note: Markop said *I know this place* and the record should have stopped dead. This is the Silent Grove. Same dead tree, same web canopy, same grey earth, same stump they stacked the loot on the night they banished the Arachnid Matriarch — a place this party cleared, on Raventree Manor's grounds, that you reached by walking. They have just re-entered it by rope, through a scarecrow's mouth, in the Shadowfell. Nobody else recognised it. One centaur with a good memory is the only reason the archive knows the Scorncrow's tree opens onto ground we already own, and Waluigi wants the obvious question printed: if that grove can be somewhere else now, what else that we cleared is still where we left it? And the Legion are standing in it.
sections.imageCaption: The Skittering Grove: webs where foliage should be, wrapped shapes hanging from the boughs like fruit, and Wario's motorbike abandoned in the roots.

outcome: No decision, and a worse position than the party started in. The Scorncrow was unmasked — human blood, at point-blank range — and escaped into its own tree. Archie killed the tree and sealed the exit; Markop shut the jaws and reopened them. Five of the party descended by rope into the Skittering Grove, where Remi and Wario were already separated and webbed, the motorbike was found but unusable, and Legion soldiers were present alongside the brood. The party is inside, split, out of magic, and unable to leave the way they came.
notableFeatures: Human blood under the Scorncrow's face — the first physical test of its 'I am not a monster' claim, and the claim held
The tree has a mouth, a throat, and a pit; every intervention made it close further
Fire magic is measurably weakened inside the Scorncrow's domain — confirmed by two failed casts before the third
Archie's all-in fire cast: eyes turned to fire, the tree died, the exit sealed
The horn on Wario's motorbike laughs in his voice at an estimated fifty-mile radius
The torch test: the pit answered in human voices — 'they're going to burn us all down'

The Skittering Grove: a web-canopied grove inside the tree, hung with wrapped beast and man

reputationNotes.remi_akamatsu_full_backstory: Pinned under the Scorncrow at point-blank range, fired a musket into its face and produced the single piece of hard intelligence the arc turns on: it bleeds human blood.
reputationNotes.archie_miser: Emptied every reserve into one fire cast that killed the tree — and sealed the party's only exit doing it. The Legion inside the grove now has an arsonist on the same side of a door that no longer opens.
reputationNotes.markop: Solved the door twice, pried the jaws, rigged the descent rope, and wrote his reasoning down.
reputationNotes.wario: Took four Murder of Crows attacks and retreated on morale, having sold the party the elixir that brought them there.
reputationNotes.dan: Went down first under the crows and spent every point he owned healing himself back onto the front of the marching order.
reputationNotes._record: Disaster Inc. came out of the night with the Scorncrow unmasked and no way home; the Iron Legion was found inside a place with one mouth and no marched route that accounts for it.

aftermath:
**Position:** the party is inside the Skittering Grove and cannot leave by the route they entered. Archie's explosion sealed the exit; Markop's bark removal shut the jaws; the rope goes down, and nothing in the record says it comes back up.

**Condition:** Archie has spent all of his magic. Feyward Dan has spent all of his on himself. Remi is webbed and separated with Wario, who has already retreated once on the log. The motorbike has been recovered and is useless — Markop is a centaur. That is a party with no reserves, no mobility, and no door.

**Intelligence gained:** the Scorncrow bleeds human blood; it opens fights by removing mobility and healers; it Shadow Jumps out of reprisal; and by Feyward Dan's estimate the party has not seen half its power. The pit contains people who can speak and who are afraid of fire. The Iron Legion is inside a place with one mouth, and nobody knows how.

**Exposure:** the horn. Fifty miles, by Archie's own estimate, into a grove the party then walked into.
waluigiAssessment:
**The archive was wrong and this filing corrects it.** *I am not a monster* was a claim, not a taunt, and the only person who ever tested it did so because she was pinned underneath it with no other options. Waluigi filed three articles calling that thing a monster. Waluigi is not going to file a fourth.

**Every door problem in this session was solved by making the door worse.** Archie burned it shut. Markop pulled a bark plate and the jaws closed. The tree responds to intervention by closing, which is not a door's behaviour — it is a throat's. The party is not besieging a fortress. They have been swallowed, and the correct model going forward is digestion, not siege.

**Feyward Dan gave the report and nobody adjusted.** *That was not half his power*, from the one man who took a full engagement from it, delivered in the same breath as *I used all of my magic*. Two facts that should have ended the plan. The plan proceeded, on a motorbike, through a mouth.

**The withdrawal was the right call and it lost to arson.** Archie proposed it: we cannot win this, run, get Dan to safety. He was correct. He then talked himself into going inside and setting the thing on fire, because that is who he is, and the archive should stop being surprised. The cost of that reversal is a split party under a sealed exit.

**The unnamed guard held the only line.** One spear, five damage, into a bold ettercap that had already webbed and reeled him. Waluigi will not invent a name for him. He would like one supplied.

**Recommendation:** find the second mouth. Something let the Legion in, the torch came back out of the trunk rather than the jaws, and voices in the pit heard a fire nobody outside could hear. There is another opening in that tree, and it is currently the party's only way home. WAH.

name: Judgement in the Grove
title: Judgement in the Grove: A Musket in the Smoke, the Warhammer That Would Not Hear an Appeal, and the Man Remi Found Asleep
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — just past midnight on the Shadowfell clock, the Skittering Grove inside the Scorncrow's tree, continuing straight out of the descent
era: Harvestide 1040 BF — Shadow Estate storm chain
location: The Skittering Grove, inside the Scorncrow's tree (Shadowfell)
status: Unresolved — the Scorncrow is dead but the grove is surrounded, Salam is down and unrecovered, Markop's skull is split, Remi is separated over a man she may have killed, and the Legion alliance ends in Archie's arrest
summary: The party fought its way out of the web canopy and into an execution. Remi swapped the crossbow for the musket and landed two direct hits through the smoke; Dan planted himself in front of everyone including Markop and turned the spiders with a mushroom-studded holy symbol; Eager and Dan killed the ettercap between them. The Iron Legion called for pest control, retreated, and then tried to arrest Archie mid-battle, which produced a temporary alliance nobody expects to hold. Markop called down divine favour, took a scythe to the skull, and split the Scorncrow's head open while it was on its knees asking a paladin for mercy. Remi, thrown clear by Mossy, found a breathing man with a red punch mark on his forehead and had the steel defender stand on his chest. Salam went down and did not get up.
description: *Three filings called the Scorncrow a monster and the fourth one took its mask off and found a human face under it. This filing is what the party did with that information. [Waluigi](#/article/waluigi) was not there. He has assembled it from [Markop](#/article/markop), [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) and a [Toad](#/article/toads) who would not give a name, and he wants it on the record before anybody smooths it over: the thing knelt, said it was human, asked a paladin to spare it, and the warhammer came down anyway. WAH.*
imageCaption: The moment before judgement. The Scorncrow on its knees with the scythe fallen out of reach, hood off, the face underneath plainly human and still asking; Markop at the top of the swing. The archive files this as neither murder nor justice.

sections.name: I. Smoke, and the Wrong Way Out
sections.imageCaption: She put the arrow back in her pocket and took the musket instead, then reloaded it slowly, in the open, with the brood already coming. Two direct hits. The bow stayed on her back.
sections.overview:
"It's a little smoky in here," Remi said.

She had been walking back the way she thought she had come, which in a grove with no sky and a silk floor is a sentence with no meaning in it. The webs take the edges off direction the same way they take the edges off sound. She got turned around once, corrected, got turned around again by the correction, and walked directly into the spiders.

She had the crossbow up and an arrow on the rail before she had finished registering the ettercap. Then she stopped. She looked at the arrow, and she looked at the thing in front of her, and she put the arrow back in her pocket.

The musket came off her shoulder instead.

The bang went flat across the web canopy and the ettercap came apart at the shoulder. A direct hit. Then she stood in the open and reloaded — powder, ball, ram, the whole unhurried procedure — while the grove watched her do it and did not close. She fired again. Another direct hit.

"You invaded my home, right," the Scorncrow said from somewhere in the dark. It was not really a question.

"Will the spiders attack?" Markop asked.

"They'll come around."
sections.waluigi_note: *She put the arrow back in her pocket. Read that again, because it is the most professional thing anybody did all night. A fourteen-year-old under contact, in smoke, having already walked into the enemy by accident, stopped to change weapons because the crossbow was the wrong tool — and then reloaded a musket in the open, twice, and hit with both. Three filings ago this girl was hiding behind Markop. Waluigi is going to stop describing her as the youngest member.*

sections.name: II. The Scythe That Cleaves Everything in Its Path
sections.overview:
The Scorncrow hurled its scythe.

It went out spinning, shrouded in something that bent the air around the blade, and it did not travel like a thrown weapon. It cleaved everything in its path — web, branch, standing bodies — and it dragged a chilling cold behind it that cut through anyone caught in the wake. Not the blade. The wake.

It caught Eager, Archie and Dan across the same line. All three took it. All three were grazed rather than opened, which is the only reason this section is four sentences instead of an obituary.

A spider came in on Eager while he was still registering the cold. Markop attacked it back off him.

Then Markop heard it: *thump. thump.* A giant green spider, going away from them rather than towards them — *thump thump* — heading for the Iron Legion guards.

Remi got webbed. "Why — *whyyyy* —" she shouted, as the strand took her and the thing on the other end of it pulled, and it clawed at her, and her clothes came apart under the hooks.

One of the Legion guards made the only correct tactical assessment of the night:

"We gotta call pest control. RETREAT!"
sections.waluigi_note: *A thrown weapon that cleaves everything in its path and freezes the air behind it, and it grazed three people instead of killing one. Waluigi notes the Scorncrow chose the spread. It could have put that scythe through a single body and it chose to open a line across three, which is what you do when you are not trying to win yet — you are trying to find out what everyone is made of. Dan said they had not seen half its power. Nobody has revised that estimate downward.*

sections.name: III. A Book in Full View, and a Paladin in Front of Everyone
sections.imageCaption: Feyward Dan put himself in front of everyone - including Markop, who is a head-and-shoulders taller and armoured - and turned the brood with a mushroom-studded holy symbol.
sections.overview:
"Come on, I'm looking at my spells," Remi said.

She said it tied up. She said it with the book open in full view, wrapped in silk, while another spider came down the strand towards her. There is no reading of that image that flatters anybody standing nearby.

Then Feyward Dan walked forward and stood in front of everyone.

Everyone including Markop — which matters, because Markop is a centaur with a warhammer and Dan is a Toad who had been unconscious an hour earlier and had spent every point of magic he owned healing himself. He put himself between the party and the Scorncrow, faced it, and then turned and swung at the spider instead.

He got out his holy symbol. A mushroom-studded thing, more garden than cathedral, and he held it up and faced it at the spiders.

Then he moved behind the spider, and he and Eager took it together — Dan swinging once, Eager coming in behind the distraction with a sneak attack. The spider roared.

Eager ran while it was distracted, straight into a spidery bush.

Markop walked past the spider. It bit at him and missed. He did not turn around to check. He was already facing the Scorncrow.
sections.waluigi_note: *Dan stood in front of Markop. Waluigi wants the ordering noted because Dan is the smallest combatant on the field and Markop is the largest, and the paladin's read was that the line goes where the oath is, not where the mass is. Four filings ago this Toad was a liability with a cursed staff. Waluigi has been unkind to him in print and is revising it here rather than quietly dropping the subject.*

sections.name: IV. Come to Offer Your Head
sections.overview:
"Oh, you come to offer your head. How vigilant."

Markop stared at him. He did not answer, which for Markop is an answer.

He walked closer. He got the warhammer up, and it began to glow — and above the dead grove with no sky in it, the ceiling opened anyway and thunder came down through it and hit the head of the hammer. Markop had come prepared. He had been holding divine favour since before the rope.

He struck. The Scorncrow blocked it. The block did not hold, and it flinched — the first time in four engagements that anything this party did has made it flinch.

Then it hit him in the head.

The scythe came around and split Markop's skull and he stood there bleeding into his own eyes, and the thing laughed at him.

"You think you can kill me? I have lived in this tree. Made it my treehouse when I was little."

Archie Miser — fireball-throwing, three-eyed, dimension-hopping, having split between worlds — prepared a fireball.

Then: "Nah, just kidding." He winked at no one in particular, and a considerably smaller firebolt hit the Scorncrow instead.

It coughed blood. "I'm still alive."
sections.waluigi_note: *Made it my treehouse when I was little. That is the second piece of physical evidence and nobody in the grove stopped moving for it. The first was the human blood under the mask. This is a childhood, in a location, with a tense. Whatever the Scorncrow is now, it is claiming to have grown up in the tree the party is currently standing inside, and Waluigi cannot file that as villain theatre because the archive already got caught doing exactly that three times.*

sections.name: V. The Tree of Love, and a Recruitment Pitch
sections.overview:
"Listen. Do you think the worst person can change?"

It was bleeding out of a ruined face and it wanted to have a conversation.

"We can hang people together on the tree of love. Join me, young one. Join the Scorncrow — or hear my last ballad."

"Sorry, Scorncrow," Archie said. "I'm on the side of good. Despite all my accidental crimes."

The guards were retreating deeper into the grove by then, and they took the opportunity of a lull in the murder to remember their jobs.

"YOU TOADS ARE UNDER ARREST."

"No — no, wait —"

"Archie Miser is right there. Arrest him."

"No, wait, *help*, get these spiders —"

What followed was a negotiation conducted at speed between people being actively eaten. They struck a temporary alliance: the Legion helps with the brood, the Toads agree, and Archie gets arrested at the end of it. Archie shrugged.

"This won't last."
sections.waluigi_note: *Do you think the worst person can change. Waluigi is obliged to note that the thing asked this question and then, two sections from now, was killed while asking a version of it again. The archive does not get to enjoy Archie's line about accidental crimes without also filing what the question was and who was asking it. Also: the Iron Legion attempted an arrest in the middle of a losing fight against a spider brood. Waluigi has no assessment. Waluigi simply wants it preserved.*

sections.name: VI. Down Here
sections.overview:
"What are you doing down here?" Archie asked.

"Down here? What do you mean?"

"Yes, *down here*. Remember the rope? We went down into the lair, and now we're fighting here. We're in the undergrowth, right?"

"The tree is a teleporter," Markop said.

"What are you guys talking about? This is the ruined manor."

Nobody resolved it. A punch landed somewhere off to the left with a sound like a wet sack dropped from height, and Wario laughed.

"I am tired of running."

"It's been like six seconds," Markop shouted.

Wario explained, without embarrassment, that he is a bad runner.

"This is all your fault, you know," Archie yelled at him.

"Alright then. I'll leave."

Salam fired at the ettercap and missed. Dan swung at the same moment and also missed. Then Feyward Dan and Eager went in together, in time with each other, and both hit, and the ettercap fell.

Every head in the grove turned to the Scorncrow.
sections.waluigi_note: *Three people in one conversation gave three different answers for where they were standing: down a rope in a lair, in the undergrowth, and in the ruined manor. Markop said teleporter. Last filing he recognised this place as the Silent Grove, which the party cleared on Raventree's grounds by walking to it in daylight. Waluigi's position is that all three answers are correct and that this is the actual emergency, well ahead of the spiders.*

sections.name: VII. BARK BARK
sections.overview:
Eager healed himself with duct tape.

Remi was about to be eaten. The thing had her wrapped and it came down to bite and there was no version of the next second that she survived on her own.

**BARK BARK.**

Mossy hit her side-on at a dead run. The steel defender put its whole weight into her and she went flying — off the strand, into the leaves and the branches, through them, and out the other side, and landed sitting on the floor of the grove with her ears ringing and every spider suddenly somewhere else.

She got up and she ran, and she kept running, and then she was alone in the woods.

She investigated. She found a body.

Then: no — he is breathing.

A man, unconscious, face up. There was a red punch mark on his forehead, fresh and clean and roughly the size of a gauntlet.

She tapped his head with a stick. Lightly. Nothing happened.

Mossy came bounding back to her.

Remi told Mossy to wake the guy up by stepping on him.

The hard steel came down and pressed onto the man's ribcage. There was a crack. The steel defender barked and lowered itself very slightly further onto his chest.

*Welp,* Remi thought. *I killed a guy in his sleep.*
sections.waluigi_note: *A red punch mark on the forehead. Waluigi has read the previous filing and would like to draw the obvious line: Wario was separated inside this grove, Wario punches things, and Wario had just announced he was tired of running. Waluigi is not filing that as fact. Waluigi is filing it as the first question anybody should ask the man if Remi's steel dog has left him in a condition to answer it.*

sections.name: VIII. The Warhammer Has Spoken
sections.overview:
Markop swung. The Scorncrow blocked with the scythe.

"Wait — please. I will change."

Its head split open and started glowing.

"Wait, please. I am human. I am not a monster."

It started to kneel.

"You're a paladin, right? You have to spare me. Please. I will change ways."

The head splits open. The warhammer has spoken and given him judgement.

Markop picked up the scythe.

Somewhere behind him, the rest of it was still going. Archie Miser announced that they should regroup to the three Toads, while pointedly not hearing the guards who were still asking to arrest him.

"We gotta find our friends."

"We're coming to get you home, Remi."

Alone in the woods with a man she may have killed, Remi heard the word *home* and it went somewhere in her that the spiders had not reached. She shook her head. Focus on the mission. Her dress was torn. She needs new armour.
sections.waluigi_note:
*Here is what the record says, in order. It said it would change. It said it was human. It said it was not a monster — the same sentence it has shouted in four consecutive engagements, the one the archive spent three filings calling theatre until a girl with a musket proved it was a statement of fact. Then it knelt. Then it asked a paladin, by his office, for mercy. Then Markop killed it.*

*Waluigi is not going to pretend this is uncomplicated and he is not going to pretend he would have done differently. The thing put a scythe through Markop's skull ninety seconds earlier and it had four engagements of dead Toads behind it. But the archive already got caught once assuming this creature was lying, and Waluigi will not make the same error in the other direction by recording an execution as a victory. Markop picked up the scythe. That is a man taking a trophy from someone who was on his knees, and Waluigi files it with the ruling and lets the reader weigh it.*

sections.name: IX. Every Grove at Once, and Salam
sections.imageCaption: Salam clawed across the face and down, crossbow fallen beside him, as the grove closes from every direction at once and Embercap's fire goes up behind. He was not recovered. The wound scars.
sections.overview:
It was not over. It was arithmetic.

Embercap, and spiders — giant spiders — came in and surrounded the grove, out of every grove, from every direction at once.

Markop felt a shadow come over him and then a blaze of heat off his own shoulder as fire went past his ear and into the ettercap.

A spider got to Salam. It clawed across his face, opened it, and he went down unconscious. It will scar.

A Legion guard was killed by a spider. At the same moment, on the other side of the grove, Markop was attacked again.

**Salam has fallen.**
sections.waluigi_note: *Salam. Last filing he crossed forty feet of open ground under a murder of crows to stabilise a man he barely knows, and said 'your service won't go in vain' to somebody who was still breathing. This filing he is face down in a dead grove with his face opened and the only healer in the party is the man he saved. Waluigi wants the symmetry on the record and wants somebody to go and get him.*

reputationNotes.markop: Executed the Scorncrow on its knees, unmasked, after it identified itself as human and formally asked a paladin for mercy. The archive is not recording that as clean, and neither are the Judges.
reputationNotes.remi_akamatsu_full_backstory: Two direct musket hits through the smoke, reloading in the open between them; armour destroyed, and she stood.
reputationNotes.archie_miser: Negotiated the temporary alliance that ends in his own arrest. The Legion took the help and served the warrant anyway.
reputationNotes.dan: Stood in front of the entire party including Markop and turned the brood with a mushroom-studded holy symbol.
reputationNotes.eager: Concerted kill on the ettercap with Dan, after a sneak attack into the distraction Dan bought him.
reputationNotes._record: The Iron Legion called for pest control, retreated, accepted an alliance, and used it to attempt an arrest mid-battle. The relationship is worse than before it started; the heavy engagement belongs on the Pressure axis, not on Standing.

aftermath:
**The Scorncrow is dead.** It was killed on its knees, unmasked, after identifying itself as human and formally asking a paladin for mercy. Markop took the scythe. The claim it made four times across four engagements — *I am not a monster* — was tested by musket last filing and found to be true, and it was killed anyway. The archive is not going to record that as clean.

**Salam is down** with his face opened and has not been recovered. Feyward Dan, the only healer on the field, spent every point of magic he owned on himself an hour ago.

**Markop's skull is split** and he continued fighting through it. **Remi** is separated in the woods, her armour destroyed, standing over an unconscious man whose ribs her steel defender has just cracked on her instruction. She believes she may have killed him in his sleep.

**The Iron Legion alliance is explicitly temporary** and ends with Archie Miser's arrest. Archie's own assessment: *this won't last.* At least one guard is dead.

**The grove is still surrounded.** Embercap and giant spiders came in from every direction as the Scorncrow fell, so killing the thing that owned the place did not empty it.

**Unresolved:** the man with the red punch mark. Where the party actually is — rope-lair, undergrowth, or ruined manor, with Markop's teleporter reading unconfirmed. And what the Scorncrow meant by growing up in a tree the party has been standing inside all night.
waluigiAssessment:
**The execution is the filing and everything else is weather.** Waluigi has written the word *monster* about that thing in three separate articles and had to retract it last filing when a fourteen-year-old put a musket against its face and found a man underneath. This filing it knelt. It said it was human. It asked a paladin, by his office, to spare it. Markop killed it and took its scythe.

**Waluigi is not calling that murder and he is not calling it justice.** The thing had four engagements of casualties behind it and had opened Markop's skull ninety seconds earlier. But the archive got caught once assuming this creature was lying, and the correction does not become free just because the creature is now dead. Both facts go in the same paragraph or neither of them is honest.

**Remi Akamatsu is not the youngest member any more and the archive should stop filing her that way.** She changed weapons under contact because the crossbow was wrong for the target, reloaded a musket in the open twice, and read her spellbook while tied up with something descending on her. She also ordered a steel dog to stand on a sleeping man until he cracked. Both of those are the same person and Waluigi declines to separate them.

**Feyward Dan stood in front of Markop.** The smallest combatant put himself ahead of the largest. Waluigi has been unkind about this Toad in print for four filings and is revising it here rather than letting it quietly lapse.

**The position is worse than when they came down the rope.** The Scorncrow is dead, and the grove is surrounded, Salam is down, Markop is bleeding from the head, Remi is separated, the exit is still sealed, and the party's allies are the people who intend to arrest one of them. Killing the landlord did not clear the building.
